SanDisk Secures Korean Materials/Parts/Equipment Allies, Accelerates HBF Development… Timeline Moved Up by Six Months

U.S. NAND flash maker SanDisk is accelerating the development of its next-generation product, High Bandwidth Flash (HBF). In the process, Korean semiconductor industry players are emerging as key allies.

SanDisk is pursuing collaboration on HBF sample production with materials, parts, and equipment (MPE) companies that possess unrivaled competitiveness in specific fields. If the HBF market grows going forward, the benefits are expected to extend to Korea's semiconductor industry as well. Whether Samsung Electronics and SK hynix will also pick up the pace on their own product development is drawing attention.

According to semiconductor industry sources on April 9, SanDisk has recently begun collaborating with select Korean semiconductor MPE companies on HBF sample fabrication. Industry sources indicate that a company with a monopoly on certain equipment used in High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) manufacturing is expected to ship sample equipment to SanDisk around early this summer.

HBF is one of the next-generation growth drivers attracting global memory semiconductor industry attention after HBM. While HBM is made by vertically stacking DRAM dies, HBF is made by stacking NAND. It is slower than HBM but offers the advantage of processing data with significantly larger capacity.

The prevailing view in the semiconductor industry is that HBF will be complementary to HBM rather than a substitute. Rather than cannibalizing each other, both markets are expected to expand. The industry projects the HBF market will begin growing in earnest around 2030.

Professor Kim Jung-ho of KAIST's Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering — often called the "Father of HBM" — stated at a February presentation on HBF technology development and commercialization strategy that "by 2038, the HBF market will be larger than the current HBM market."

According to SanDisk's website, on August 6 of last year (local time), the company partially revealed its future roadmap in a post titled "Beyond the Memory Wall: The Inside Story of SanDisk HBF for AI Inference." It projected HBF samples would ship in H2 of this year, with HBF-based AI device samples emerging in early 2027.

An industry source said, "As sample production ramps up in earnest, SanDisk appears set to pull its previously announced HBF development roadmap forward by roughly six months," adding, "This reflects the strength of SanDisk's determination to lead the market."

Industry observers note that SanDisk's push to accelerate HBF development is also influenced by its identity as a pure NAND flash company. Without HBM — which is made from DRAM — in its portfolio, the analysis is that SanDisk is going all-in on capturing this new market.

Among Korean memory semiconductor companies, SK hynix is the most proactive on HBF. SK hynix signed an MOU with SanDisk in August of last year to pursue HBF standardization. In February of this year, the company announced it held a kickoff event for an HBF spec standardization consortium at SanDisk's U.S. headquarters.

However, the SK hynix–SanDisk collaboration is focused on establishing HBF standards and has not yet progressed to the stage of joint mass production. Both companies are expected to develop and bring their own products to market independently.

SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung stated at the company's annual general meeting on March 25, "We will proactively secure next-generation portfolios including Processing-in-Memory (PIM), Compute Express Link (CXL), and HBF, and leap forward as a 'Full-Stack AI Memory Creator' that proposes more than what customers want."

An SK hynix spokesperson said, "Beyond what was announced around February regarding HBF standardization efforts with SanDisk, we are unable to confirm specific details of the development roadmap."

Samsung Electronics has not publicly disclosed any HBF roadmap or development plans. However, according to industry sources, Samsung is also reportedly preparing for HBF development.$SNDK

세계 최초 광자 양자컴퓨터 순수 플레이 상장 기업, Xanadu$XNDU.
Nature 논문 3편을 디바이스 레벨로 분석했습니다.

• 양자 우위? 증명됨. 단, 벌크 광학으로. (chip이 아닌)
• 칩 집적? 됨. 단, loss가 56%.
• 결함허용 큐빗? 구조는 확인. 단, 점수가 합격선의 1/16.

결론: 물리는 작동하는 걸 보였지만, fault tolerance까지 loss를 40배 줄여야 한다. 현재 동작점은 Xanadu가 만든 threshold 그래프에 찍히지도 않는 수준입니다.

광학 양자컴퓨터가 그렇듯, 이 회사의 기업가치도 결국 광학 소자의 loss 개선 속도에 수렴합니다.

무료 공개이며, 양자컴퓨팅 투자에 관심 있으신 분들 참고하세요.

Xanadu ($XNDU) is the only publicly traded pure-play photonic quantum computer company.

I read their 3 Nature papers as a Si-photonics engineer and broke down what matters:

• Borealis (2022): 36μs vs 10⁹ years. Quantum advantage proven, but bulk optics only.

• Aurora (2025): 35 chips, 86.4B modes. But P1 path loss is 56%. The fault tolerance graph can't even fit the current operating point on its axes.

• GKP (2025): 0.62 dB vs 9.75 dB threshold. Same chip, reduce loss from 18% to 0.5%, and you cross the line.

Three papers, one conclusion: the technology works. It is not yet fault-tolerant. The gap is measured in dB.
